blocks.content: The Chairman and other members of the UPSC are appointed by the President of India and hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) consists of a Chairman and other members appointed by the President of India.
The Constitution does not specify the exact strength of the Commission, leaving it to the discretion of the President.
At least one-half of the members of the Commission must be persons who have held office for at least ten years either under the Government of India or under the Government of a State.
Members hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier.
The Chairman or any member can resign at any time by addressing their resignation letter to the President of India.
The Constitution does not prescribe any specific qualifications for UPSC members, except for the requirement that half of the members must have 10 years of prior government service.
The strength of the UPSC is not fixed by the Constitution; it is determined periodically by the President.
Conditions of service of the Chairman and members are determined by the President and cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.
